problems: The new ChIP evidence supports occupancy by TCF7L2, JUND, and YY1 in HCT116, but does not distinguish which TF mediates a variant effect. SP1 and CTCF also have HCT116 regional occupancy evidence; none of these results demonstrates allele-specific binding.

The chain field allele_binding_more is set to ref, but the cited evidence does not establish that the ref allele binds more. The binding claims correctly avoid asserting a direction; the ref assignment remains unsupported.

EH38E3858447 is open in HCT116, but accessibility and pELS annotation do not demonstrate that this variant changes enhancer activity. The MYC contacts in E06 make it a candidate target, not a functionally established target; the same element has links to other genes and no reported CRISPR perturbation.

The colorectal-cancer association does not show that any nominated TF–element–MYC path mediates disease risk. The catalog entries also report different effect alleles for colorectal-related traits (E07), so a direction-specific mechanistic claim is not established.

critique.next_experiment: Create isogenic HCT116 G and T alleles (or precisely edit the endogenous site), then measure allele-specific TF occupancy and expression of MYC and other linked genes. Combine this with separate acute perturbations of TCF7L2, JUND, and YY1 to test which factor, if any, makes the variant-dependent regulatory effect.
